articles.summary: 3D Systems Announces Agreements to Exchange All Outstanding 5.875% Convertible Senior Secured Notes Due 2030, Eliminating All Secured Debt Rachael Dalton… Wed, 11/04/2026 - 21:08 Release Date Wednesday, Nov 4, 2026 9:08 PM ROCK HILL, South Carolina, November 4, 2026 – 3D Systems Corporation (NYSE: DDD) (“3D Systems” or the “Company”) today announced that it has entered into separate, privately negotiated exchange agreements with all of the holders (the “Transaction Participants”) of its currently outstanding 5.875% convertible senior secured notes due 2030 (the “2030 Notes”). Pursuant to these exchange agreements, the Company has agreed to exchange $92,030,000 aggregate principal amount of 2030 Notes held by the Transaction Participants, representing all of the outstanding 2030 Notes, for $85,000,000 aggregate principal amount of newly issued 3.30% convertible senior notes due 2031 (the “2031 Notes”), 13,471,138 shares (the “Shares”) of the Company’s common stock and $20,000,000 in cash, plus accrued and unpaid interest on the exchanged 2030 Notes to, but excluding, the closing date, subject to certain adjustments if the closing occurs after December 1, 2026 (the “Exchange”). The 2031 Notes will be senior unsecured obligations of the Company, will bear interest at a rate of 3.30% per year, payable semiannually in arrears on April 1 and October 1 of each year, beginning on April 1, 2027, and will mature on April 1, 2031, unless earlier converted, redeemed or repurchased. The 2031 Notes will be convertible into cash, shares of the Company’s common stock or a combination of cash and shares, at the Company’s election, at an initial conversion rate of 291.3753 shares of common stock per $1,000 principal amount of 2031 Notes (equivalent to an initial conversion rate of approximately $3.43 per share of common stock, which represents a premium of approximately 30.0% over the last reported sale price of the Company’s common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on November 4, 2026 of $2.64 per share), subject to certain adjustments. The Exchange is expected to close on or about November 12, 2026, subject to certain closing conditions. Assuming all of the 2030 Notes are exchanged, upon the closing of the Exchange, no 2030 Notes will be outstanding, and the Company expects that the indenture governing the 2030 Notes will be satisfied and discharged and the related guarantees and the liens on the collateral securing the 2030 Notes will be released. 3D Systems will not receive any cash proceeds from the Exchange. This announcement is neither an offer to sell nor a solicitation of an offer to buy any of the Shares, the 2031 Notes or any shares of common stock issuable upon conversion of the 2031 Notes, nor shall there be any offer, solicitation or sale in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under applicable securities laws. The offer and sale of the Shares, the 2031 Notes and any shares of common stock issuable upon conversion of the 2031 Notes have not been, and will not be, registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or qualified under any state securities laws and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from such registration or qualification requirements. Since then, that same spark continues to ignite the 3D Systems team as we work side-by-side with our customers to change the way industries innovate. Video production timelines are reduced approximately 10x, from days to hours. Sponsors maintain full control of production, review and launch processes, whilst all sponsor-confidential information is stored within ICON's secure environment. With over half a million site users worldwide, and over five million clinical study related trainings delivered via the platform, FIRECREST creates a consistent operating model for site engagement across a Sponsor’s portfolio. The new AI-directed video engine leverages a rich library of proven content and templates, developed over more than 25 years of ICON’s experience creating study communications with its FIRECREST platform. The platform's first application supports site selection and feasibility activities, converting study-specific information into engaging site selection videos that help investigator sites quickly understand research opportunities and study requirements. “Clinical trials rely on effective communication with investigator sites,” said Brian Mallon, Executive Vice President, Site & Patient Solutions at ICON plc. “Video is a powerful communication format, and ICON’s AI-directed video engine removes cost and complexity, and is far faster than traditional video production, enabling sponsors to scale communication and deliver greater site engagement and message consistency, whilst maintaining governance and reducing risk”. Employer Payroll Taxes: Costs, Due Dates, and Forms Explained

What payroll taxes do employers pay, and how much can they add to the cost of an employee? In this video, you’ll learn the major employer payroll tax responsibilities, including employee income tax withholding, FICA taxes, FUTA, and state unemployment taxes. The video also explains how employer payroll tax costs can add to employee compensation, how deposit schedules work, and how Form 941, Form 940, and W-2 reporting fit into the process. Use the Employer Payroll Tax Calculator to estimate employee costs or review the complete Guide to Payroll Taxes.

Topics:

  • 0:00 - What Payroll Taxes Really Cost an Employer
  • 0:28 - Payroll Taxes vs. Income Taxes
  • 0:55 - Withholding, FICA, FUTA, and SUTA
  • 2:03 - Adding Up the Employer's Share
  • 2:20 - When Payroll Taxes Are Due
  • 2:42 - Deposits vs. Filings: The Forms To Know
  • 3:18 - How Paychex Can Help
  • 3:54 - Wrap Up

<p id="transcript-button">View Transcript</p>

What Payroll Taxes Really Cost an Employer

0:00 If you hire someone for $60,000, they’ll actually cost you closer to $65,000. That extra money? Payroll tax.

0:09 And it isn’t one tax. It’s four. Get them right, and nobody notices. Get them wrong, and the IRS definitely does. But you don’t need to be a tax expert. You just need to know what you owe and when it’s due.

Payroll Taxes vs. Income Taxes

0:28 First, what is payroll tax? It’s federal and state tax tied to your employees’ wages. Income tax applies to all kinds of income. Payroll taxes apply only to wages and salaries, and they fund Social Security, Medicare, and unemployment. That’s payroll taxes vs. income taxes. Now, the four.

Withholding, FICA, FUTA, and SUTA

0:55 One: income tax withholding. Your employee’s W-4 tells you how much to hold back. They pay it. You collect it and send it in.

1:06 Two: FICA. That’s Social Security tax and Medicare. Your employee pays 6.2% and 1.45%, and you match both, dollar for dollar. Social Security tax has a cap. Medicare has no cap. And for pay over $200,000, you withhold an extra amount.

1:33 Three: FUTA, federal unemployment tax. This one’s all yours. It’s 6% on the first $7,000 of wages, but a state credit can drop it to 0.6%. That’s $42 per employee.

1:53 Four: SUTA, state unemployment tax. It works like an insurance premium. Your state sets your rate based on your claims history.

Adding Up the Employer's Share

2:03 What does that add up to? For one employee earning $60,000; your share runs roughly $4,700 to $4,900 a year. About 8% on top of salary.

When Payroll Taxes Are Due

2:20 So, when are payroll taxes due? That depends on your payroll tax deposit schedule. Had $50,000 or less in liability during the IRS lookback period?

2:34 You deposit monthly. More than that? Semiweekly, days after each payday.

Deposits vs. Filings: The Forms To Know

2:42 Paying on time is half the job. The other half? Showing your work. That’s what filings are for. They report what you withheld and what you paid.

2:55 Every quarter, Form 941 covers income tax withholding plus both halves of FICA. Once a year, Form 940 handles FUTA. And at year-end, each employee gets a W-2 showing their wages and withholding.

3:14 That’s a lot to track every pay period.

How Paychex Can Help

3:18 Paychex helps automate payroll taxes by calculating, filing, and paying your federal, state, and local taxes for you. It’s designed to keep you ahead of filing deadlines, supports multi-state compliance, and can help you find tax credits that put money back in your business. It’s included in most Paychex payroll packages.

3:45 Our tech handles the math, and real people have your back, with 24/7 support whenever you need it.

Wrap Up

3:54 Want to see your numbers? Try the employer payroll tax calculator below and get the full Employer’s Guide to Payroll Taxes to learn how to calculate payroll taxes step by step.

4:06 And subscribe for more guidance on payroll, HR, and everything in between.

articles.summary: FREMONT, Calif., November 5, 2026 – Spectral flow cytometry leader Cytek Biosciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: CTKB) today announced that its Cytek Aurora® Evo system has been named Drug Discovery Innovation of the Year in the 2026 BioTech Breakthrough Awards. The annual program recognizes innovative companies, products and services across the life sciences and biotechnology industries. As pharmaceutical companies and contract research organizations (CROs) expand the use of high-parameter spectral flow cytometry in drug discovery and applied research, they face growing demands for sample throughput, automation and consistent data across instruments and research sites. The Cytek Aurora Evo system builds on the established performance of the Cytek Aurora® platform with enhancements designed to help laboratories scale complex research workflows without compromising data quality. “The Cytek Aurora Evo system is helping transform life sciences research by addressing the growing need for higher throughput, greater automation and reproducible data,” said Bryan Vaughn, Managing Director, BioTech Breakthrough. “By bringing these capabilities together without compromising flexibility or data quality, the system helps pharmaceutical and CRO laboratories scale high-parameter spectral flow cytometry across increasingly complex research workflows.” Built on Cytek’s Full Spectrum Profiling™ (FSP®) technology, the Aurora Evo system combines an advanced optical and electronics architecture with high acquisition speed and automated features. For workflows using plate wells, acquisition time has been reduced by approximately 40% compared with earlier generations. Automated startup and shutdown reduce operator intervention and extend instrument utilization beyond the workday, allowing laboratories to make greater use of instrument capacity. The platform is also being developed to provide a path toward automated sample processing using robotic arms. These improvements can help laboratories increase screening capacity and make more efficient use of instrument time, particularly when managing large sample volumes and time-sensitive studies. The system also incorporates instrument harmonization to support more consistent, reproducible results across systems, laboratories and time. This is particularly important when pharmaceutical companies and CROs transfer assays between locations, where minimizing instrument-to-instrument variability can help researchers compare results with greater confidence. “Modern drug discovery requires technologies that support increasingly complex experiments while helping laboratories work more efficiently and generate consistent, reliable data,” said Wenbin Jiang, Ph.D., CEO of Cytek Biosciences. “The Cytek Aurora Evo system addresses these needs by combining higher throughput and automation with the proven performance and reproducibility of the Cytek Aurora platform. This recognition reflects our continued commitment to advancing flow cytometry to meet the evolving needs of researchers.” For more information, please visit https://cytekbio.com/pages/aurora-evo. About Cytek Biosciences, Inc. Cytek Biosciences (Nasdaq: CTKB) is a leading cell analysis solutions company advancing the next generation of cell analysis tools by delivering high-resolution, high-content and high-sensitivity cell analysis utilizing its patented Full Spectrum Profiling™ (FSP®) technology. Cytek’s novel approach harnesses the power of information within the entire spectrum of a fluorescent signal to achieve a higher level of multiplexing with precision and sensitivity. Cytek’s platform includes: its core FSP instruments, the Cytek Aurora®, Northern Lights®, Cytek Aurora® CS and Cytek Aurora® Evo systems; the Muse® Micro system; the Cytek Orion™ reagent cocktail preparation system; the Enhanced Small Particle™ (ESP™) detection technology; the flow cytometers and imaging products under the Amnis® and Guava® brands; and reagents, software and services to provide a comprehensive and integrated suite of solutions for its customers. Cytek is headquartered in Fremont, California with offices and distribution channels across the globe. More information about the company and its products is available at www.cytekbio.com. Cytek’s products are for research use only and not for use in diagnostic procedures (other than Cytek’s Northern Lights-CLC system and certain reagents, which are available for clinical use only in China and the European Union). HR Compliance Checklist: 7 Key Areas Employers Should Review

HR compliance touches everything from hiring and pay practices to leave, benefits, recordkeeping, and employee policies. In this video, discover seven HR compliance checkpoints employers can review to help identify potential gaps. The video also walks through a simple HR compliance audit built around relevance, consistency, and documentation. For deeper guidance, explore the complete HR compliance guide or explore Paychex HR consulting for personalized HR and compliance support.

Topics:

  • 0:00 - Could Your Business Pass an HR Compliance Check?
  • 0:10 - How Compliance Gaps Usually Start
  • 0:23 - The 7 HR Compliance Checkpoints
  • 2:19 - A Quick Audit You Can Run This Week
  • 2:48 - How Paychex Can Help
  • 3:14 - Wrap Up

<p id="transcript-button">View Transcript</p>

Could Your Business Pass an HR Compliance Check?

0:01 - Could your business pass an HR compliance check today? Most owners think yes. Then they find the gap. And here’s the thing: most businesses don’t get into trouble on purpose. They get there through a missed update, an outdated process, or a document that wasn’t where it should’ve been.

How Compliance Gaps Usually Start

0:20 - So let’s fix that. HR compliance comes down to seven checkpoints. Run through these and you’ve covered much of your risk.

The 7 HR Compliance Checkpoints

0:29 - One: Hiring. Compliance starts before anyone’s hired. Consistent processes, fair candidate evaluation, and EEOC anti-discrimination hired. Consistent processes, fair candidate evaluation, and EEOC anti-discrimination rules protect you — and get you better hires. Two: Wage and hour. Misclassifying an employee as a contractor, or exempt when they’re not, remains one of the most common compliance risks out there. Track time accurately and know the difference. Three: Safety and workplace policies. This is about keeping people safe and setting clear expectations — OSHA duties, harassment prevention, workplace conduct. And document all incidents, because if it’s not documented, it’s hard to prove it happened. Four: Leave and accommodations. FMLA, ADA, paid leave. Handle every request the same way, every time. When the process is clear, employees feel genuinely supported. Five: Benefits and payroll. These are the things employees see every single pay period — payroll taxes, required notices, retirement plans. Get them right and you build real trust. Six: Recordkeeping. If anything’s ever questioned, your files are your defense — payroll records, hiring records, I-9s, performance notes. Keep them complete. Seven: The employee handbook. It ties everything together — policies, leave, pay practices, workplace expectations. And it should reflect how your business actually operates, not how it ran three years ago.

A Quick Audit You Can Run This Week

2:20 - Here’s a fast check you can do this week. Take those seven checkpoints and ask one question of each: is this current, consistent, and documented? That mini-HR compliance audit surfaces most of the gaps hiding in a business.

2:37 - Now, the catch: all seven of these keep changing. Regulations shift; policies age out. That's exactly why businesses are moving away from doing it themselves.

2:50 - Paychex pairs 50-plus years of HR expertise with AI-powered technology that helps monitor requirements and flag potential gaps before they become costly. Have a question about an employment law? You can get a real-time answer instead of digging through regulations yourself.

3:09 - And when things get complicated, there's a real expert by your side when you need one.

Wrap Up

3:15 - So don’t wait for a gap to find you. Run that quick audit this week and get the full HR compliance guide at the link below. And don’t forget to subscribe for more HR guidance.

(NYSE: ARDT) ("Ardent Health" or the "Company"), a leading provider of healthcare in growing mid-sized urban communities across the U.S., today announced results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Third Quarter 2026 Operating and Financial Summary All comparisons are versus the same prior year period. See the footnotes to the Operating Statistics table of this press release for definitions of the metrics below and a full list of key operating metrics. Total Revenue $1.62 billion Net Income Attributable to Ardent Health $45 million Adjusted EBITDA(1) $138 million Adjusted EBITDAR(1) $180 million Admissions 0.1% growth Y/Y Adjusted Admissions 2.9% growth Y/Y Operating Cash Flow $122 million Increasing 2026 Adjusted EBITDA Guidance Reaffirming Total Revenue: $6,400 - $6,700 million Raising Adjusted EBITDA midpoint(1): $500 - $535 million (1) Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDAR are financial measures that have not been prepared in a manner that complies with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles ("GAAP"). See "Supplemental Non-GAAP Financial Information" and reconciliations of non-GAAP measures to their most comparable GAAP financial measures contained later in this press release. Third Quarter Results Reflect Improving Performance; Raising 2026 Adjusted EBITDA Guidance "We delivered strong third quarter results, highlighted by adjusted EBITDA of $138 million, a 4% reduction in SWB expense, and 2.9% adjusted admissions growth," said Dave Caspers, President and Chief Executive Officer of Ardent Health. "Our performance reflects disciplined execution, with volumes improving sequentially and continued progress on our operating priorities. IMPACT initiatives continued to gain traction and remain on track to achieve at least $70 million of savings this year, contributing to greater efficiency and stronger financial performance." "We enter the fourth quarter with confidence in the trajectory of our business and ability to execute on the opportunities ahead," Caspers continued. "Based on our year-to-date performance and continued operational momentum, we are raising our 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint 1.5%." “Consistent with our focus on disciplined portfolio management, we entered into a definitive agreement during the third quarter to transition full ownership of our Kansas hospital to our joint venture partner,” Caspers noted. “We expect this transaction to enhance margins while allowing us to redeploy capital toward growth in core markets where we can build scale and integrated systems of care.” “We remain focused on strategic capital deployment that prioritizes organic investments and M&A," said Caspers. “The company’s $766 million of cash and 2.5x lease-adjusted net leverage provide flexibility to execute against these priorities while maintaining a balanced approach to capital allocation that creates long-term shareholder value.” Financial Performance Summary For the third quarter of 2026: Total revenue grew 3.1% year-over-year to $1,625 million. The growth in total revenue consisted of a 2.9% increase in adjusted admissions. Net income attributable to Ardent Health was $45 million, or $0.31 per diluted share, compared to net loss attributable to Ardent Health of $23 million, or $0.17 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was $138 million, which includes benefits from IMPACT program initiatives, improving volume trends, and operational execution. Operating Performance Summary The following table provides a summary of certain key operating metrics for the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same prior year period. See the footnotes to the Operating Statistics table of this press release for definitions of the metrics below and a more extensive list of key operating metrics. Balance Sheet, Cash Flow & Liquidity Update; $25 Million Increase To Share Repurchase Program As of September 30, 2026, the Company had total cash and cash equivalents of $766 million and total debt of $1.1 billion. Year-to-date net cash provided by operating activities was $258 million, or an increase of 5% compared to $247 million in the same prior year period. During the third quarter of 2026, the Company repurchased 1.0 million shares of its common stock for $11 million. Ardent’s Board of Directors has authorized a $25 million increase to its share repurchase program. Supplemental Non-GAAP Financial Information We have included certain non-GAAP financial measures in this press release, including Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA margin, and Adjusted EBITDAR. We define these terms as follows: Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income plus (i) provision for income taxes, (ii) interest expense and (iii) depreciation and amortization expense (or EBITDA), as adjusted to deduct noncontrolling interest earnings, and excludes the effects of loss on extinguishment and modification of debt; other non-operating losses; recoveries from the cybersecurity incident in November 2023 (the "Cybersecurity Incident"), net of incremental information technology and litigation costs; certain legal matters and related costs; enterprise restructuring costs; exit and acquisition-related costs; enterprise resource planning system conversion costs; equity-based compensation expense; and loss (income) from disposed operations. Adjusted EBITDA margin is defined as Adjusted EBITDA divided by total revenue. Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin are non-GAAP performance measures used by our management and external users of our financial statements, such as investors, analysts, lenders, rating agencies and other interested parties, to evaluate companies in our industry. Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin are performance measures that are not prepared in accordance with GAAP and are presented in this press release because our management considers them important analytical indicators commonly used within the healthcare industry to evaluate financial performance and allocate resources. Further, our management believes that Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin are useful financial metrics to assess our operating performance from period to period by excluding certain material non-cash items and unusual or non-recurring items that we do not expect to continue in the future and certain other adjustments we believe are not reflective of our ongoing operations and our performance. Because not all companies use identical calculations, our presentation of Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures of other companies. While we believe these are useful supplemental performance measures for investors and other users of our financial information, you should not consider Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin in isolation or as a substitute for net income or any other items calculated in accordance with GAAP. Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin have inherent material limitations as performance measures, because they add back certain expenses to net income, resulting in those expenses not being taken into account in the performance measures. We have borrowed money, so interest expense is a necessary element of our costs. Because we have material capital and intangible assets, depreciation and amortization expense are necessary elements of our costs. Likewise, the payment of taxes is a necessary element of our operations. Because Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin exclude these and other items, they have material limitations as measures of our performance. Adjusted EBITDAR . Adjusted EBITDAR is defined as Adjusted EBITDA further adjusted to add back rent expense payable to real estate investment trusts ("REITs"), which consists of rent expense pursuant to the master lease agreement (the "Ventas Master Lease") with Ventas, Inc. ("Ventas"), lease agreements with Ventas for 18 medical office buildings and a lease arrangement with Medical Properties Trust, Inc. ("MPT") for the Hackensack Meridian Mountainside Medical Center. Adjusted EBITDAR is a commonly used non-GAAP valuation measure used by our management, research analysts, investors and other interested parties to evaluate and compare the enterprise value of different companies in our industry. Adjusted EBITDAR excludes: (1) certain material noncash items and unusual or non-recurring items that we do not expect to continue in the future; (2) certain other adjustments that do not impact our enterprise value; and (3) rent expense payable to REITs. We operate 30 acute care hospitals, 12 of which we lease from two REITs, Ventas and MPT, pursuant to long-term lease agreements. Additionally, we lease 18 medical office buildings from Ventas pursuant to lease agreements with initial terms of 12 years and eight options to renew for additional five-year terms. Our management views the long-term lease agreements with Ventas and MPT, as more like financing arrangements than true operating leases, with the rent payable to such REITs being similar to interest expense. As a result, our capital structure is different than many of our competitors, especially those whose real estate portfolio is predominately owned and not leased. Excluding the rent payable to such REITs allows investors to compare our enterprise value to those of other healthcare companies without regard to differences in capital structures, leasing arrangements and geographic markets, which can vary significantly among companies. Our management also uses Adjusted EBITDAR as one measure in determining the value of prospective acquisitions or divestitures. Finally, financial covenants in certain of our lease agreements, including the Ventas Master Lease, use Adjusted EBITDAR as a measure of compliance. Adjusted EBITDAR does not reflect our cash requirements for leasing commitments. As such, our presentation of Adjusted EBITDAR should not be construed as a performance or liquidity measure. Because not all companies use identical calculations, our presentation of Adjusted EBITDAR may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures of other companies. While we believe this is a useful supplemental valuation measure for investors and other users of our financial information, you should not consider Adjusted EBITDAR in isolation or as a substitute for net income or any other items calculated in accordance with GAAP. Adjusted EBITDAR has inherent material limitations as a valuation measure, because it adds back certain expenses to net income, resulting in those expenses not being taken into account in the valuation measure. The payment of rent is a necessary element of our valuation. Because Adjusted EBITDAR excludes this and other items, it has material limitations as a measure of our valuation. This metric represents the total number of hospitals operated by us at the end of the applicable period, irrespective of whether the hospital real estate is (i) owned by us, (ii) leased by us or (iii) held through a controlling interest in a JV. This metric includes the managed clinical operations of the hospital at UT Health North Campus in Tyler, Texas ("UT Health North Campus Tyler"), a hospital owned by The University of Texas Health Science Center at Tyler, an affiliate of The University of Texas System. Since we only manage the clinical operations of UT Health North Campus Tyler, the financial results of such entity are not consolidated under Ardent Health, Inc. (2) Licensed beds (at period end). This metric represents the total number of beds for which the appropriate state agency licenses a facility, regardless of whether the beds are actually available for patient use. (3) Utilization of licensed beds. This metric represents a measure of the actual utilization of our inpatient facilities, computed by (i) dividing patient days by the number of days in each period, and (ii) further dividing that number by average licensed beds, which is calculated by dividing total licensed beds (at period end) by the number of days in the period, multiplied by the number of days in the period the licensed beds were in existence. (4) Admissions. This metric represents the number of patients admitted for inpatient treatment during the applicable period. (5) Adjusted admissions. This metric is used by management as a general measure of combined inpatient and outpatient volume. Adjusted admissions provides management with a key performance indicator that considers both inpatient and outpatient volumes by applying an inpatient volume measure (admissions) to a ratio of gross inpatient and outpatient revenue to gross inpatient revenue. Gross inpatient and outpatient revenue reflect gross inpatient and outpatient charges prior to estimated contractual adjustments, uninsured discounts, implicit price concessions, and other discounts. The calculation of adjusted admissions is summarized as follows: Adjusted Admissions = Admissions x (Gross Inpatient Revenue + Gross Outpatient Revenue) Gross Inpatient Revenue (6) Inpatient surgeries. This metric represents the number of surgeries performed on patients who have been admitted to our hospitals. Pain management, c-sections, and certain diagnostic procedures are excluded from inpatient surgeries. (7) Outpatient surgeries. This metric represents the number of surgeries performed on patients who have not been admitted to our hospitals. Pain management, c-sections, and certain diagnostic procedures are excluded from outpatient surgeries. (8) Emergency room visits. This metric represents the total number of patients provided with emergency room treatment during the applicable period. (9) Patient days. This metric represents the total number of days of care provided to patients admitted to our hospitals during the applicable period. (10) Total encounters. This metric represents the total number of events where healthcare services are rendered resulting in a billable event during the applicable period. This includes both hospital and ambulatory patient interactions. (11) Average length of stay. This metric represents the average number of days admitted patients stay in our hospitals. (12) Net patient service revenue per adjusted admission. This metric represents net patient service revenue divided by adjusted admissions for the applicable period. Net patient service revenue reflects gross inpatient and outpatient charges less estimated contractual adjustments, uninsured discounts, implicit price concessions, and other discounts.
